prompt: Create exactly one isolated whole cultivated orange carrot plant (Daucus carota subsp. sativus), a botanical game model reference. Input 1 is ONLY the approved gongbi watercolor surface/style master, NOT leaf anatomy; input 2 gives miniature Jiangnan world style, NOT composition; input 3 is a real-photo growth montage for anatomy ONLY. Chinese gongbi light-colour painting adapted to a coherent three-dimensional object: clear selective fine moss-green/umber outlines and structural vein lines, restrained sage/jade green pigment washes, subtle ink mottling, rounded natural volume, matte. Keep fine organized linework visible for texture generation, avoid photorealism, plastic, glossy rubber, yellow antique filter, black ink holes. Full isolated plant with coherent three-dimensional radial volume, clear near/far overlap, weak-perspective three-quarter angle 25 degrees above the horizon, every tip visible with 15% margins, flat neutral pale-gray background. NO scene, soil, pot, hands, labels, symbols, text, collage, other plants, detached pieces or strong cast shadows. No flowers, seeds, wild-carrot white umbels or purple roots. STAGE: juvenile early storage-root growth, referencing panels C and D. ONE small slim pale-orange tapered taproot, about 4–5 times longer than its diameter, with a short slender pale tip, and FOUR sparsely arranged, individually clear compound green leaves radiating from its shoulder on thin petioles. The overall crown is airy with plenty of empty spaces, leaf stems upright and outward, some project forward and some behind; not a flat fan. Foliage above root is about twice the root length. Render complete root for later burial in game, with a few restrained painted horizontal fine marks and no hairlike tangled roots. No giant mature root and no dense mature foliage.
review: Initial broad/planar leaf candidate not submitted; revised narrow divided foliage, stage-specific root size and crown density. Geometry and soil clearance still require actual P2 checks.
